prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
## Main story

At first, the conflict looked like a direct military crisis. By September, it was starting to look like a much longer struggle, with shipping, energy, and diplomacy under pressure.

The conflict began on February 28, 2026, when the United States and Israel started air strikes on Iran.

On June 14, the two sides agreed to a ceasefire memorandum. Four days later, the sea blockade was lifted. But the pause did not last.

In July, Iran attacked three merchant ships outside approved routes. The blockade began again on July 14.

After that, the pressure continued in several areas. An Iranian petrochemical plant stopped production. An Iranian opposition media group also reported a large loss of natural gas production capacity, although that figure has not been independently confirmed.

At the same time, the US Navy found more than 100 objects believed to be mines in a shipping area of the Strait of Hormuz.

Diplomacy also failed to open a clear path forward. On August 18, President Trump said that no talks with Iran were scheduled. The 60-day period for negotiations then ended without an agreement.

A private political-risk group moved its expected time for easing tensions from September to the end of the year. On September 4, one report said that a month-long quiet period was ending and that the region was moving back toward a dangerous and increasingly unsustainable stalemate.

Still, the picture is mixed. A senior US energy official said that oil traffic through the strait had reached its highest wartime level on one day. That claim points in the opposite direction.

【Point One】
The two oil figures measure different things. The US energy secretary said that more than 17 million barrels passed through the strait on September 1. But official quarterly data show an average of only about 5 million barrels a day in the second quarter, down from about 20 to 22 million before the war. A busy day does not prove that the wider damage has ended.

【Point Two】
The deeper surprise is that economic pain has not yet created an exit. A plant stopped, mines were found, and reports described lost gas capacity. But no talks were scheduled, the deadline passed, and the peace forecast moved later. Pressure can grow without producing a settlement or a clear time for one.

point_one.reasoning: 戦時中の単日の通過量と、戦争前後の四半期平均を具体的に対比し、高い一日の数字だけでは海峡全体の物流被害が回復したとは言えないと示している。Full Storyにあった一日の好材料を、長期的なデータとの比較によって解釈し直しており、新しい理解を加えている。

point_two.reasoning: 経済的損害が拡大しても交渉や合意につながらないという示唆は明確で、記事固有の工場停止・機雷・ガス生産減少・交渉期限を使っている。ただし、Full Storyがすでに示した『複数分野の圧力にもかかわらず外交が進まず、緊張緩和の見通しが後退した』という中心結論をほぼ言い換えており、聞き手への実質的な追加価値は限定的である。
